claims.quote: WW domain-containing oxidoreductase (WWOX) is known as one of the risk factors for Alzheimer's disease (AD), a neurodegenerative disease.

claims.object_text: binds Tau via C-terminal SDR domain
claims.quote: WWOX binds Tau via its C-terminal SDR domain

claims.object_text: interacts with ERK, JNK, and GSK-3β
claims.quote: interacts with Tau phosphorylating enzymes ERK, JNK, and GSK-3β

claims.object_text: severe neural diseases and early death
claims.quote: Loss of WWOX in newborns leads to severe neural diseases and early death.

claims.object_text: accumulation of extracellular amyloid beta plaques
claims.quote: accumulation of extracellular amyloid beta plaques

claims.object_text: age-related increases in pS14-WWOX promotes neuronal degeneration
claims.quote: Age-related increases in pS14-WWOX accumulation in the brain promotes neuronal degeneration.

Suppression of Ser14 phosphorylation by a small peptide Zfra leads to enhanced protein degradation, reduction in NF-κB-mediated inflammation, and restoration of memory loss in triple transgenic mice for AD.

claims.object_text: p53 and WWOX counteraction leads to upregulation of AD-related protein aggregation in brain and lung
claims.quote: tumor suppressors p53 and WWOX may counteract each other in vivo, which leads to upregulation of AD-related protein aggregation in the brain and lung.

claims.object_text: stronger binding to partners suppresses cancer growth and reduces inflammation
claims.quote: the stronger the binding between WWOX and its partners, the better the suppression of cancer growth and reduction in inflammation.

claims.object_text: stronger complex formation with partners may better block AD progression
claims.quote: the stronger complex formation between WWOX and partners may provide a better blockade of AD progression.
